# AI rules — Serverless proxy (Node.js on Vercel)

Scope: `api/**` — the CORS proxy that the browser calls as `/api/proxy?url=…` in production. No database, no
session, no secrets. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) §4.2 for where this sits; the client side of the
call is covered in [AI_FRONTEND.md](AI_FRONTEND.md).

## Function shape

- One ES module per endpoint, `export default async function handler(req, res)` (`package.json` is
  `"type": "module"`). No npm dependencies: use the built-in `fetch` and `Buffer`.
- Run `node --check api/<file>.js` after every edit. `npm run dev` does not run `api/`, so a behaviour change
  can only be tried on a Vercel deployment (or `vercel dev`), not on the local server.

## Input

- Accept `GET` only; answer anything else with `405`.
- Require the `url` query parameter, parse it with `new URL`, and fetch only `http:` / `https:` addresses.
  Reject everything else with `400` before any request is made.

## Output

- Compare the upstream `Content-Type` against the exact allowlist in the file. Anything not on it is sent as
  `application/octet-stream` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`.
- Always send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- Add a type to the allowlist only when client code consumes it, and say which code in the commit or the
  design note.
- Return errors as JSON `{ error }` with a fitting status code. Pass the upstream status through when the
  provider answers with a failure.
